newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso reins in losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso reins in losses at close.

text.p: The Mexican peso considerably pared earlier weakness at the close on Monday due to local dealers selling long dollar positions, traders said.
"There is a lot of money in the market, but no real demand. The same dealers who stepped in to buy dollars in the morning sold long positions in the afternoon," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart closed 0.7 and 0.8 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.8820/7.8870 and 7.8770/7.8820 per dollar.
The same-day peso closed earlier 6.05 centavos weaker at 7.9030/7.9080 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso had weakened to 7.9190/7.9250 per dollar in early trade.
Earlier pressure on the peso was put down to Wednesday's maturity of US$1.5 billion in Cetes-Libor bonds issued by the Mexican government one year ago.
Holders may chose between the highest of two rates, 12-month Libor or Cetes less 600 basis points, payable in dollars or pesos, respectively.
"Volume was heavy until midday, and the forthcoming maturity of the government debt issue may have been the reason," said a trader.
Traders said the peso may weaken further on Tuesday, due to dealers squaring month-end positions and to cover other dollar positions prior to U.S. markets being closed for Thanksgiving on Thursday.
